solutionReview.headline: The vertex of a downward parabola is its maximum: $x={{h}}$.
reasoning: The coefficient $-{{a}}$ is negative, so the graph opens downward and its vertex is the highest point.
The square $(x-{{h}})^2$ is 0 at $x={{h}}$: $-{{a}}({{h}}-{{h}})^2+{{k}}={{k}}$. Any other $x$ subtracts a positive amount from {{k}}.
So the greatest revenue is predicted at $x={{h}}$.
solutionReview.commonError: Choosing a nearby value: the maximum is exactly where the squared term is 0.

solutionReview.headline: $x={{future}}$ is outside the data range $0\le x\le {{maxx}}$: extrapolation.
reasoning: The model was fitted on $0\le x\le {{maxx}}$, and ${{future}}>{{maxx}}$.
Predicting outside the observed range is extrapolation; the pattern in the data may not continue there.
